validity.array_size_assumed: 256 axons x 256 neurons per core, 4096 cores, 64x64 mesh
validity.notes: Characterized at the 0.8 V corner, where akopyan2015truenorth Fig. 17 publishes a THREE-POINT firing-rate sweep at fixed synaptic density -- the only published TrueNorth data that separates marginal switching energy from static power. The chip operates over 0.70-1.05 V with a 42-323 mW envelope; points at other voltages are outside this corner because no voltage-scaling model is published. Temperature is not stated by either paper.

area_per_cell.derivation: One TrueNorth synapse is one bit of the core SRAM crossbar (merolla2014a S1: 'w_ij in {0,1} ... We implement the 256x256 w matrix as a crossbar'), and that SRAM uses a published 0.152 um^2 6T bitcell. Bitcell only: excludes decoders, sense amps, drivers and the redundant rows/columns.
area_per_cell.note: The papers publish no SRAM macro area, so this is the storage cell alone; per-core area is declared separately and is the number to trust for whole-chip area.

conductance_levels.note: Binary digital synapse: w_ij in {0,1}. Effective weight precision comes from the per-neuron 9-bit signed value selected by one of 4 axon types, not from the cell.

write_sigma.derivation: TrueNorth stores synapses in digital 6T SRAM, so a written weight has no analog programming spread. Zero is a fact about the technology, not a missing measurement.

read_sigma.derivation: Digital SRAM read; no analog column-current sensing, so no read spread.

area_per_adc.derivation: The core is fully digital (scheduler, token controller, core SRAM, neuron, router). There is no analog-to-digital converter in the datapath, so the count is zero by construction rather than unknown.

e_adc_conversion.derivation: No ADC exists in a TrueNorth core; see area_per_adc.

t_adc_conversion.derivation: No ADC exists in a TrueNorth core; see area_per_adc.

area_per_neuron_logic.derivation: The neuron block is a published 2900 um^2 (1272 gates incl. the PRNG) time-multiplexed 256 ways: 2900 / 256 = 11.328 um^2 per neuron. The paper's own effective figure, 2900/256 + 3.0 = 14.3 um^2, is this value plus the state storage declared as area_per_state_bit.

area_per_state_bit.derivation: Published: 'storing neuron state (20 bits) requires an additional area of 3.0 um^2 per neuron'. 3.0 / 20 = 0.15 um^2 per bit. Cross-check: this lands within 1.3% of the independently published 0.152 um^2 6T bitcell (akopyan2015truenorth Section V-E), so the two area facts agree.

bytes_per_connectivity_entry.citation: akopyan2015truenorth Section V-E, p.1546 (core SRAM row fields)
bytes_per_connectivity_entry.derivation: A neuron's routing declaration occupies the 26-bit spike-destination field plus the 4-bit delivery-tick field of its core SRAM row = 30 bits, which is 4 bytes on the wire (the spike packet is likewise 32 bits).
bytes_per_connectivity_entry.note: This replaces the framework's global 4/8/16 B modelled band for this target: TrueNorth's wire format is published.

t_program_per_byte.derivation: Configuration enters through the scan chain, published at 10 MHz with no PLL or global clock tree. A scan chain shifts one bit per cycle: 1 / 10 MHz = 100 ns per bit, so 8 bits = 800 ns per byte.
t_program_per_byte.note: Assumes a single serial scan path at one bit per cycle. If the chip shifts several chains in parallel the true figure is lower by that factor; the papers do not state the chain count.

t_cycle.citation: merolla2014a p.4; akopyan2015truenorth Section III p.1540 and Section VII p.1551
t_cycle.note: The nominal 1 ms tick is the chip's defining real-time step ('a global 1 kHz clock'). The low corner is the fastest demonstrated operation, 21x real-time (1 ms / 21 = 47.6 us), which depends on activity, synaptic density and voltage; 5x real-time (200 us) was verified bit-exact against software. There is no faster-than-nominal guarantee, so the band is one-sided.

area_global_fixed.citation: merolla2014a p.6; akopyan2015truenorth Fig. 1 caption p.1538
area_global_fixed.derivation: Die is 4.3 cm^2 = 430 mm^2; the 4096 cores occupy 4096 x (240 x 390 um) = 383.4 mm^2. The balance, 430 - 383.4 = 46.6 mm^2 (10.8% of the die), is the periphery outside the core array: merge-split, I/O ring and pads.

p_static_per_core.derivation: The intercept of the same two-endpoint fit: P_static = 68 mW - 2.297 pJ x 1.5541e9 events/s = 64.43 mW at 0.8 V, divided by 4096 cores = 15.73 uW. Cross-check against the independently published zero-activity corner of 42 mW at 0.70 V: leakage scales super-linearly with supply, and 42 x (0.8/0.7)^2 = 54.9 mW to 42 x (0.8/0.7)^3 = 62.7 mW bracket this intercept without the fit having used it.
p_static_per_core.note: Includes the 1 kHz tick baseline, not leakage alone.

p_static_global.derivation: The whole 42 mW zero-activity corner is already attributed to p_static_per_core across the 4096 cores. Declaring any of it again here would double count the same measurement.

area_per_core_total.citation: akopyan2015truenorth Fig. 1 caption p.1538; merolla2014a Fig. 2 caption p.14
area_per_core_total.note: 'one core occupies 240 x 390 um of silicon' — the measured complete-core footprint (crossbar SRAM, neuron block, scheduler, token controller, router together). Supersedes the decomposed area constants; the per-cell and per-neuron figures remain declared for decomposition studies but are never summed with this.

e_mac.derivation: MARGINAL energy per synaptic event, by linear regression on the published 0.8 V sweep at 128 synapses/neuron: 68 mW @ 11.58 Hz, 71 mW @ 20.07 Hz, 94 mW @ 95.93 Hz. Event rate = 1048576 neurons x rate x 128. Fitting P = P_static + E x events on the two ENDPOINTS gives E = (94-68) mW / (1.28742e10 - 1.5541e9) events/s = 2.297 pJ; the held-out middle point then predicts 70.62 mW against a published 71 mW (-0.54%).
e_mac.note: This is the WHOLE-CHIP marginal cost of one more synaptic event -- array read, neuron update and spike routing together -- which is why e_inter_tile_hop is deliberately not declared: adding it would charge routing twice. It is NOT the published 26 pJ/synaptic-event, which is whole-chip power divided by the event rate at one operating point and therefore already contains static power (see truenorth.md).

host_compute_rate.derivation: identity: a measured host wall is used at face value (wall / 1.0)
host_compute_rate.note: The derate a MEASURED host wall is divided by. Identity by definition: this framework measures its host ComputeOp walls end-to-end on the deployment host (StageTimer), and derating a measurement would invent headroom. [H5] Declared here after the loihi precedent because its absence refused the record-plane e2e/energy headlines BY NAME on runs whose host wall was in fact measured.
